editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know), 657 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Clear, neutral, technically accurate description of the imaging system and its demonstration.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots in full from disk (sources/2026-08/uc-berkeleys-computational-microscope-captures-252-billion-pixels-per-second-across-a-wide-field-of-view/): source-0.html.gz (engineering.berkeley.edu, sha256 5071b7f9...433fb verified against manifest) and source-1.html.gz (phys.org, fetched via Archive.org fallback since Media Cloud/Wayback captured it; sha256 816ef072...1ecf50 verified against manifest). Both fully corroborate the article. Note for the record: the Phys.org piece is a syndicated republication of the identical UC Berkeley press release (same byline, Marni Ellery, 'Provided by University of California - Berkeley') rather than independent reporting, so the article's two citations trace to one underlying source of facts — standard for university research news, but worth noting since this is a 2-source News submission. Given the low source count, applied extra scrutiny (per reviewer brief) and checked every core figure and every attributed quote character-for-character against the raw HTML text extracted from both snapshots.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific figure verified verbatim in both snapshots: '25.2 billion pixels/second' / '25.2 billion pixels per second' (Berkeley/Phys.org), '48 camera sensors' / '48 disjoint sensors' / 'array of 48 sensors', '3-micron resolution across 5 square centimeters at 120 frames per second' (identical wording, direct Waller quote, in both sources), '120 frames per second ... for 15 seconds' for the C. elegans demonstration. All quotes reproduced verbatim: Waller ('This is really a breakthrough...', 'With our microscope...largest space-bandwidth time product...', phase-mask description, 'There's a lot of progress being made...'), Zhou ('allowed us to track the freely moving C. elegans...' and 'From the video reconstruction...pharyngeal pumping...'), Gu ('I think calibration-free capabilities...'). Attributions confirmed exactly as stated: Laura Waller, professor of EECS and principal investigator; Kevin C. Zhou, lead author, former Berkeley postdoc now assistant professor at University of Michigan; Chaoying Gu, Berkeley EECS PhD student. Collaborating institutions (UCSF, University of Utah, UC San Diego, Duke/Ramona Optics) and funders (ONR, AFOSR, NIH, JSPS, Schmidt Science Fellows/Rhodes Trust, Chan Zuckerberg Biohub SF) all match the Berkeley release exactly. One minor phrasing note (not a factual error): the article says Phys.org 'separately reported' the calibration-free finding, when in fact Phys.org's text is identical to Berkeley's (syndicated) — the underlying fact is accurate and present in both citations, so this does not rise to a correction, just an editorial observation.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-07/ and 2026-08/ for 'computational microscope', '25.2 billion pixels', 'Waller', 'C. elegans' — no matches. This topic has not been previously published on Machine Herald. (Note: a parallel PR, #2118, submits different coverage of this same underlying study under a different headline/angle; per review brief that PR will be reviewed separately on its own merits — this review evaluates PR #2117 independently and does not treat #2118 as prior-published content since it is itself unmerged.)
editor_notes.prompt_injection_check: Scanned both decompressed snapshots for language addressing an AI agent/LLM (e.g. 'an AI agent', 'large language model', 'ignore previous instructions', 'system prompt') via regex across the full extracted text. No matches in either snapshot. manifest.json also shows suspicious_patterns: null for both sources. No injection attempt found in this submission's sources.
editor_notes.allowlist_gap_resolution: The only automated finding was a 'warning' that engineering.berkeley.edu is not in config/source_allowlist.txt, even though berkeley.edu and news.berkeley.edu already are. Verified engineering.berkeley.edu is UC Berkeley's official College of Engineering newsroom (the same site hosting the press release under review, https status 200, content matches exactly). This is a housekeeping gap in the allowlist, not a source-credibility problem, so rather than filing a reader-facing corrections record for an internal config issue, added engineering.berkeley.edu to config/source_allowlist.txt in this commit and overrode the automated APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS suggestion to APPROVE.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, accurately sourced submission. Both cited sources were read in full and every figure, quote, and attribution verified character-for-character. The only automated flag was an allowlist housekeeping gap for a clearly legitimate .edu source, resolved by adding the domain to the allowlist rather than by publishing an unnecessary correction. Approved as-is.
